title: Redwood Migration Demo: OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Nimbus through API parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood, demoed the Console and Optimize recommendations, discussed VPC/private deployment, KMS, benchmarks and next steps for a pilot including a 48-hour throughput test.
topics: Private deployment, VPC, KMS, SOC2 compliance
Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching & quantization
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-25 15:00 UTC | Duration: 57 minutes | Attendees: Evelyn Park, Marco Sanchez (Redwood); Lina Cho, Ben Harper, Raj Patel (Nimbus)

[00:00] Evelyn: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh I'm Evelyn from Redwood, i'll hand it to Marco to kick off the technical demo, but quick agenda: parity map from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together into Redwood API, Console walkthrough, Optimize suggestions, and Q&A.

[00:18] Marco: thanks Evelyn, hi Lina, Ben, Raj, nice to meet you all. quick check, you mentioned you're running chat completions with OpenAI, embeddings against Anthropic for search, and a few models from Together for lower-cost endpoints, is that right?

[00:31] Lina: yep that's right. we've got a mix — ChatGPT for customer-facing chat, Claude for internal summarization, and Together models for bulk batch generation. trying to reduce token costs and get more predictable latency for peak times.

[00:47] Ben: also we have streaming in prod for the chat UI, and function calls for retrieval augmentation, so parity for streaming + tool-calling is a hard requirement.

[01:02] Marco: totally, and we'll show the Redwood API surface that maps to those. note: there's some auto-transcription quirks on our side, so if names get munged — apologies — we'll clarify.

[05:12] Marco: demo start — here's a simple generate endpoint on Redwood: POST /v1/generate — for chat-style you pass messages, for completions you pass prompt, for streaming you set stream=true and we return chunked events. So mapping is pretty straightforward from OpenAI: chat.completions -> /v1/generate with messages, and embeddings have their own /v1/embeddings route.

[07:05] Ben: can you show function calling? how close is that to OpenAI's calling schema?

[07:22] Marco: sure. function calling works similarly — you declare functions in the request, Redwood will emit structured responses; we also have an option to return a JSON schema and validated output. small difference: we put an explicit content_type header when you want strict JSON parsing, but payloads map 1:1 in practice.

[10:40] Raj: any gotchas when migrating Together models? we use a few 7B and 13B quantized versions for cost reasons.

[10:55] Marco: good question — Together models usually quantize differently; Redwood supports common quantization profiles and we'll recommend configs via Optimize. For Dedicated or Private we can push quantized variants with the same model name, and the runtime will pick optimized kernels. sometimes tokenization differences appear — we suggested a quick tokenization compare test in the first pilot.

[15:03] Evelyn: switching to the Console — you'll see per-route dashboards, latency percentiles, token cost breakdown, and trace links. this is where Platform teams usually head to validate SLA compliance and to tune batching.

[15:35] [screen share sound — brief pause] Marco: here's an example routing policy — you can route by latency SLO (we'll send to Dedicated) or cost tier (fallback to hosted cheaper variant). we use labels like model.variant.quant for routing.

[19:10] Ben: curious about embeddings. Anthropic embedding outputs differ slightly in dimensionality — do we need to reindex?

[19:25] Marco: if dimensionality differs, yes you'll need to reindex, but Redwood supports parallel bulk-embed pipelines and incremental reindexing. we typically recommend running a small sample set to compute cosine similarities and confirm parity before a full reindex.

[22:40] Lina: security questions — we need VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, SOC 2 type II, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. do you support all of that?

[22:55] Evelyn: yes — Private deployment supports VPC and on-prem options; KMS/HSM integrations available, and audit logs can ship to your SIEM. we have SOC2 docs we can share; Marco will drop links.

[26:10] Raj: latency — during peaks we see 99p latency spikes to 1200ms with current provider. can Redwood meet sub-500ms for 2k RPM?

[26:27] Marco: depends on model and sequence length; for typical chat payloads with 2k RPM we suggest Dedicated with autoscale and prefix caching; with our kernel selection and KV cache we've seen median <200ms and 99p around 450-600ms on similar workloads. we'll run a benchmark with your payloads to validate.

[30:00] Ben: any migrations for rate limits and retries? we have client-side backoff tuned for OpenAI's 429s.

[30:12] Marco: retry semantics are similar; we expose headers for quota usage and a plugin for SDKs to map rate limit errors. you can also configure per-route throttles in the Console to avoid client-side thrashing.

[33:45] Evelyn: Optimize — quick demo: the Optimize tab suggests batching window tweaks, recommends quantization profile per model and flags prompts where responses vary across model variants. helps keep unit costs down.

[36:00] [brief cross-talk — someone typing] Lina: do you have pre-written parity guides? like a mapping table from OpenAI fields to Redwood fields?

[36:18] Marco: yes we'll send a parity spreadsheet — examples: openai.chat.create -> /v1/generate with messages array; openai.createEmbedding -> /v1/embeddings; streaming uses SSE-ish chunked events. we'll include a diff with sample curl and python snippets.

[40:05] Raj: pilot shape — what's minimal to validate? we want real traffic, cost delta, and latency metrics.

[40:20] Evelyn: typical pilot: 48-72 hour throughput test against Dedicated or a Private single-node, with your traffic replay (we can accept a sanitized trace), and two evaluation prompt sets to check quality parity. runbook: pre-migration tokenization check, 1-2 day benchmark, reindex embeddings if dims change.

[43:32] Ben: for function calls we rely on exact JSON output for our router — how strict is Redwood's validation?

[43:47] Marco: we have a strict mode that validates against JSON schema and rejects malformed outputs; by default we also return the raw text for debugging.

[46:55] Lina: cost modeling — can you give a rough % improvement moving Together quantized models into Dedicated, assuming similar ONNX profiles?

[47:10] Marco: rough numbers: Dedicated plus quantization + batching can yield 30-60% unit cost reduction depending on utilization; Optimize will produce a more tailored estimate after we see your workload.

[50:00] [pause] Evelyn: ok, let's capture next steps — i'll send the parity guide, Marco will schedule a capacity planning call, and we'll set up a pilot.

[50:25] Lina: timeline — we want pilot next sprint, ideally start by 2026-04-01. is that doable?

[50:40] Evelyn: yes, we can aim to have infra ready by 04/01. we'll confirm with a follow-up calendar invite.

[51:00] Raj: legal/procurement — we need an NDA and SOC2 before data sharing, can you send procurement contacts?

[51:12] Evelyn: yes, i'll send SOC2 and the NDA template, also link to our data processing addendum.

[53:20] Ben: okay thanks, that demo was helpful, we'll review parity doc and send sample traces.

[55:00] Evelyn: great, thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pricing/sizing spreadsheet and next meeting invite. bye.

[56:00] (end)

Note: transcription flaws present — e.g., "Console" occasionally transcribed as "Consol", some model names garbled in a few places.
